correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge4\), the proof treats every target type relative to a fixed probe and constructs a shortest path avoiding an arbitrary nonincident edge. The only delicate matched target has at least six length-three candidates, or an explicit alternative when the deleted edge is incident with that target. Thus every probe monitors exactly its incident edges and the DEM family is exactly the vertex-cover family. The independent-set classification gives the polynomial and the unique two minimum covers. The standalone verifier recomputes distances after each edge deletion and exhaustively checks all subsets for \(4\le n\le7\), while confirming the \(n=3\) exception.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural stability question for a standard dense bipartite perturbation of a foundational exact family. The sharp failure at \(n=3\) makes the threshold substantive. For \(n\ge4\), the structural theorem identifies every feasible monitoring set, not only the minimum, and the polynomial isolates exactly how deleting the perfect matching enlarges the set family while leaving the optimum unchanged.
